site.name: Connecting Ridge CR1 (NASA notional study point)
site.coordinate_frame: ME/DE421 body-fixed, planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude, following cached LOLA labels; equivalence to source coordinate frame not demonstrated. ASSUMED: NASA section 7.3.3 and Figure 0.1 do not specify the frame realization or latitude type for this tuple.
site.surface_elevation_reference: Height above the 1737.4 km LOLA reference sphere, LDEM_80S_20M V2.0, bilinear at the published point interpreted in ME. Rounded to 0.1 m. Absolute vertical accuracy and source-frame equivalence are not established. No local RDR shot consistency check performed. See data/terrain/connecting-ridge-cr1_site_elevation_report.json.
site.horizons_altitude_reference: Height above the Horizons reference body for the Moon: a 1737.4 km sphere (response header 'Center radii'), the same reference as LOLA heights. Submitted 2026-11-14 (milestone 4C).
site.altitude_conversion_note: horizons_site_altitude_km = (surface_elevation_m + observer_height_above_surface_m) / 1000 = (1941.8 m + 1 m) / 1000 = 1.9428 km. Both heights are relative to the same 1737.4 km sphere, so no datum conversion is needed. Rounding: the bilinear LDEM_80S_20M surface is 1941.8206 m; it was rounded to 0.1 m (1941.8 m) before forming the Horizons altitude, so the submitted point is 0.9794 m above the interpolated surface (nominal 1 m, 0.0206 m lower). The terrain horizon uses the same submitted point (r = 1737.4 km + 1942.8 m), so Sun/Earth directions and skyline refer to one observer. No absolute vertical accuracy of the surface value is claimed; no local LOLA RDR shot consistency check was made at the site point; the nearest 20 m DEM pixel has no LOLA shot (interpolated height). Horizons echo (all 12 responses): Center geodetic 222.6, -89.468, 1.9428 exactly; Center cylindric Dxy 16.14983 km and Dz -1739.268 km equal the submitted point rounded to the printed 5 and 3 decimals, so |r| (177 mm above 1737.4 + 1.9428 km as printed) confirms the radius only to about +/-0.5 m, the printed precision of Dz near the pole.

position_conventions.azimuth: degrees clockwise from local north: N=0, E=90, S=180, W=270
position_conventions.elevation: degrees relative to the plane perpendicular to the reference-surface local zenith
position_conventions.apparent: airless apparent direction of target body center (light-time, gravitational deflection, stellar aberration)
position_conventions.time_scale: UTC (Horizons UT; after 1962 UT means UTC)
position_conventions.observer_body: Moon (301), MEAN_ME frame, east-longitude positive, reference sphere radius 1737.4 km
position_conventions.observer_altitude: site altitude above the 1737.4 km sphere = LOLA surface elevation + observer height above surface (see site.altitude_conversion_note)

horizon.processing_notes: Smooth-horizon approximation (Stage 1): 0 deg at every azimuth, i.e. the local horizontal plane of the reference-sphere observer. Terrain is NOT modeled; real local horizons near the lunar south pole can be several degrees high and would block low Sun/Earth directions.

Terrain horizon (Stage 2) from LOLA LDEM_80S_20M (pixel spacing 20 m at the pole, 20.00 m at the site) and LDEM_75S_60M (60 m pixels, used only where a ray leaves the 20 m product). Observer 1 m (nominal) above the LOLA surface: Horizons altitude 1.9428 km above the 1737.4 km sphere, formed from the surface rounded to 0.1 m, so the eye is 0.9794 m above the bilinear DEM surface; the skyline uses that same point. Geometry: great-circle rays every 0.1 deg in the Moon-fixed ME frame; apparent elevation atan2(r_t cos(theta) - r_o, r_t sin(theta)) with exact sphere geometry, so lunar curvature is counted once; negative horizons are kept. Ray sampling (distinct from the DEM pixel spacing): the DEM is bilinearly interpolated at points every 5 m along the ray to 2 km, then every 10 m; sampling finer than a pixel follows the interpolated surface and adds no terrain detail. Observer cell: the observer's foot is the same bilinear surface that is sampled (eye 0.98 m above it) and the first sample is at 5 m; no skyline point was found closer than 50 m, and ignoring terrain within 20-300 m changed the skyline by at most 4.051 deg. This is a statement about the DEM surface only: ground relief smaller than the DEM resolves, rocks and the lander are not represented. Search extent: each ray stops only when terrain at 10873 m (global LOLA maximum 10773 m (LDEM_64 label) + 100 m) could no longer rise above the running maximum; stop distances 91-203 km. A ray that leaves both products first gives null (unknown), never flat: 0 of 3600 azimuths are unknown. Horizon -0.83 to 4.11 deg, set by terrain 0.05-0.5 km away. Numerical sensitivity (max |change|): 0.02 deg azimuth step 0.004 deg; 2.5/5 m ray sampling 0.087 deg; 60 m product everywhere 2.72 deg. Site-position sensitivity scenarios (observer moved 100 m due north, east, south and west of the published point; scenarios, not a measured coordinate uncertainty or confidence interval): skyline change up to 4.154 deg in one direction; demo-window Earth-visible share up to -6.0 percentage points; Sun-visible share up to +42.2 percentage points and longest darkness up to -141.7 h relative to the nominal point. An independently implemented pixel-sweep check on the same DEM has no comparison bin where the horizon is set >= 2 km away (the skyline is set within 480 m, where a 0.25 deg bin holds few pixel centres); its same-direction check (ray at the azimuth of the highest pixel minus that pixel) gives -0.051 to +5.999 deg; a separately written near-field check (bilinear surface within 1 km, spherical-trig positions, vector geometry) reproduces the 3600 azimuths set there within 2.2e-09 deg. That checks the implementation, not the DEM. Every azimuth's skyline is set by DEM relief within 480 m of the point (a few 20 m pixels), so this horizon is NOT robust: it depends strongly on the DEM resolution, on interpolated pixels and on the exact position (see the scenarios above). Comparisons with LOLA laser shots are consistency checks against the DEM's own source data, not independent terrain validation. Shot counts (LDEC) are quality indicators, not accuracy guarantees. Regional DEM-based visibility for the published coordinate, not actual lander operating conditions. Details: data/terrain/connecting-ridge-cr1_terrain_horizon.json and data/terrain/connecting-ridge-cr1_horizon_crosscheck.json.

search_extent.stopping_rule: stop when e(R + h_max, theta) < running maximum
search_extent.h_max_basis: global LOLA maximum 10773 m (LDEM_64 label) + 100 m

resolution.note: radial_step_m is the ray sampling distance; dem_pixel_m is the terrain pixel spacing. Heights between pixel centres are bilinear interpolation, so the terrain detail is set by the pixel spacing (and by LOLA ground-track density), not by the ray sampling.

setting_points.note: Terrain sample that sets each azimuth's horizon. shot_count = LOLA shots in the nearest DEM pixel (LDEC); 0 means that height is interpolated between ground tracks. Shot counts are quality indicators, not accuracy guarantees.

checks.lola_shots_note: Consistency check: the LDEM was gridded from LOLA RDR shots through 2017-02-02, and 100 % of these shots predate that cutoff, so this is not independent terrain validation.
checks.azimuth_convention_note: Sanity check only: one direction (ME +X) vs the 60-day mean Horizons Earth azimuth, which libration moves by several degrees. It rules out gross errors (mirrored or rotated azimuths, tens of degrees), not sub-degree offsets.

site_shift_scenarios.note: Sensitivity scenarios, not a measured coordinate uncertainty or confidence interval: the observer moved 100 m due north, east, south and west of the published point (eye kept 0.98 m above the DEM at the new point). Changes are relative to the nominal point, for the fixed demo windows (14 days from 2026-12-05 + 0/1/3/7 d), terrain mode.
